head.pub: cd07fdf (wf10/uxdec: the round, the merge of dev 22c93f4 at 0fe9fd7, four reconciliations, the handoffs)

summary: Verification 4: an independent replay of every decision on a fresh production build of the merged head (dev M6.2 to M6.4 merged into wf10/uxdec), on Chromium, desktop WebKit and the iPhone 13 emulation, with the same harness as verification 3 plus a tour of the M6 dev routes and a check of the M6 entries' names and the blob demo's tier (c) marks. Verdicts: 25 verified, 1 partly (D22, as before), 5 unchanged as required (D3, D14 outcome, D29, D30, D31), 0 not, 0 regressed: the merge regressed nothing. Every fact that failed also failed in verification 3 for the same pre-existing reason (24 px standalone links, the 26 px checkbox), except D23 on WebKit and iPhone, where the review machine's headless WebKit now draws about 3 frames a second and verification 3's own build fails the same way today (a control run; UXDEC-VER4-01). Sweep: 335 routes in 874 states, no route failed to open, no sideways overflow, clipped text, serious or critical axe issue, rendered 'TODO' or score wording. A plain production build holds no dev route and no Transformers.js or ONNX Runtime code. Two new findings, neither a regression.

decisions.notes: Owner's words on the rendered #/privacy in all three engines: 'HumanBench collects no personally identifiable information, and all responses are anonymous.' ('In short'); no 'TODO' in the rendered text or the title of the static notice, the server notice (?hb_backend=...#/privacy), the server data page, the welcome or the gate; no controller, contact or draft-terms placeholder. Static-build truth on the merged head: during welcome -> gate -> honour -> device -> ready -> Begin -> skip -> one answer every http(s) request went to the page's own host only ({"own":"127.0.0.1:4781","foreign":[]}), and the autosave appeared in localStorage; the notice says 'Nothing is sent to a server', names what the web host sees, and calls the online version a plan with consent asked again first. Server variant: random identifier, consent as the basis, 24 months as the plan, deletion naming the weekly backups (eight weeks) and the archive, the two-day hashed network address. Axe 0 serious light and dark; 320 px and 200% text: no overflow, no clipped text; the same 24 px 'Back' and 'Privacy and terms' standalone links as verification 3 (app.css .hb-standalone-link min-height 24 px, unchanged; the only failed facts of D1, ["privacy 320 px: no target under 44 px","privacy 200% text: no target under 44 px"]). Two whole ?fast=1 sessions per engine (no skips; Spatial skipped) completed in all three engines with the one break before Working Memory, and no later part grew after the skip (journey.json files). new_findings.summary: Headless WebKit on the review machine (desktop WebKit and the iPhone 13 emulation) now delivers about 3 animation frames a second to the refresh probe (the device screen reads '3 Hz'; the RT self-test reads 30.3 Hz, 60 Hz at verification 3), so the 60-frame measurement that D23 starts on the gate cannot finish during a person's pace through the gate and honour screens, and the device screen shows 'Checking your screen' for 149 ms (WebKit) and 240 ms (iPhone) before Continue is enabled; Chromium is as at verification 3 (2 ms, no text, 60 Hz). The same test against verification 3's own build gives the same numbers today, and web/src/session is byte for byte the verified head, so this is the environment, not the merge or the product.
new_findings.suggestion: None for the product. For the record: re-run D23 on WebKit on another machine or in real Safari when convenient; the harness's 300 ms bound is a property of a 60 Hz environment.

new_findings.summary: On the blob demo's M1-like profile at 390 px (five or more spokes not measured, D13 B) the not-measured tier (c) skills, Emotion Reading and Creative Thinking, are named in the 'Not measured: ...' list under the chart without their ◇, while at 1280 px their chart labels carry the ◇ and 'not measured', and the table rows carry the ◇ and the tier (c) wording at both widths. Dev's M6 test wanted the glyph on those labels 'measured or not'; the reconciled test follows D13 B. Seen in Chromium and WebKit.
new_findings.suggestion: A line for the viz owner: accept (the table keeps the mark), or carry the glyph into the stub list (a product change in BlobChart.svelte / stubListText).
